function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**What the “triangulation metrics” function does** The `requests_get` function you’re looking at is a helper that talks to the *Triangulation API* to pull a quick snapshot of how many triangulation runs have been executed for each product‑branch pair over a recent window of time. In plain English: | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Return a list of all product/branch combinations that have had at least one triangulation run in the last N days (default = 90). | | **Return format** | A JSON array where each element looks like:
`{ "product_id": , "branch_id": , "run_count": }`
So you can see how many runs were performed for each combination. | | **Parameters** | • `days`: Number of days back from today to consider.
• `end_date`: Optional override for the “today” reference point (`YYYY‑MM‑DD`).
• All other arguments (`headers`, `cookies`, `auth`, etc.) are standard HTTP options that let you add authentication tokens, set content‑types, use proxies, etc. | | **Typical use case** | You want a quick health check: “Which products/branches are still active?” or “Did we hit our run quota this month?” | --- ### Example call ```python response = requests_get( url="https://api.example.com/triangulation/metrics", params={"days": 30}, # Look back 30 days instead of the default 90 headers={"Accept": "application/json"}, cookies={"session_id": "abc123", "auth_token": "def456"} ) data = response.json() print(data) ``` If the API responds with: ```json [ { "product_id": 101, "branch_id": 1, "run_count": 12 }, { "product_id": 102, "branch_id": 2, "run_count": 7 } ] ``` you now know that product 101’s branch 1 ran 12 times in the past month, while product 102’s branch 2 ran 7 times. --- ### Why it matters - **Monitoring** – Spot inactive branches early (zero `run_count` means no activity). - **Capacity planning** – See which branches consume the most resources. - **Reporting** – Feed the output into dashboards or alerting systems. That’s the essence of the “triangulation metrics” endpoint: a lightweight way to audit recent triangulation activity across your entire product portfolio.
